items.name: Firecrawl Agent
items.description: AI-powered autonomous extraction. The agent navigates sites and extracts structured data (takes 2-5 minutes).

items.name: Firecrawl Alexandria
items.description: Alexandria brings ready-made website workflows, API providers, and specialized indexes into Firecrawl search and scrape. Semantic discovery finds capabilities by the data you need; domain matching connects web results to tools that may retrieve richer structured data beyond the page. Discover a tool that fits the task and get structured results directly, reducing the browsing, parsing, and repeated requests needed to assemble the data yourself.

items.name: Firecrawl Crawl
items.description: Bulk extract content from a website. Crawls pages following links up to a depth/limit.

items.name: Firecrawl Developer Index
items.description: For official documentation, setup, examples, migrations or compatibility, follow [official documentation](references/official-documentation.md). Continue below for implementation or bug evidence beyond the docs. Reuse adequate evidence when switching approaches.

items.name: Firecrawl Download
items.description: > **Experimental.** `download` is available under the `firecrawl x` command group.

items.name: Firecrawl Interact
items.description: Interact with scraped pages in a live browser session. Scrape a page first, then use natural language prompts or code to click, fill forms, navigate, and extract data. For web searches, use `search` — interact is for acting on a specific page.

items.name: Firecrawl Map
items.description: Discover URLs on a site. Use `--search` to find a specific page within a large site.

items.name: Firecrawl Monitor
items.description: Detect when content on a website changes and get notified by webhook or email. Firecrawl handles fetching, diffing, judging, and notifying server-side. Each page in a check is labeled `same`, `new`, `changed`, `removed`, or `error`.

items.name: Firecrawl Parse
items.description: Turn a local document into clean markdown on disk. Supports **PDF, DOCX, DOC, ODT, RTF, XLSX, XLS, HTML/HTM**.

items.name: Firecrawl Research Index
items.description: Find the research papers that answer a research query. Some questions have a single answer; many have several — and when in doubt, lean toward returning the fuller relevant set (most relevant first) rather than narrowing to one. A reader is better served seeing the neighboring methods and papers than having them silently dropped.

items.name: Firecrawl Scrape
items.description: Read a URL for page content, or execute a selected provider tool for structured data. Discover tools with `search` and inspect their inputs with `list` before execution. Multiple URLs can be scraped concurrently.

items.name: Firecrawl Search
items.description: Search naturally using the user’s actual question. Default search returns web results plus relevant Alexandria tools, with optional web content scraping.

items.name: Firecrawl
items.description: Search, scrape, and interact with the web. Returns clean markdown optimized for LLM context windows.

items.name: Venice Api Keys
items.description: Admin endpoints for managing Bearer API keys. Management routes need an **ADMIN** key. For wallet-only auth, use [`venice-auth`](../venice-auth/SKILL.md) / [`venice-x402`](../venice-x402/SKILL.md) instead.

items.name: Venice Api Overview
items.description: Venice AI is an OpenAI-compatible inference platform for text, image, audio, video, embeddings, and typed decisions. One API - two ways to pay: a traditional **API key** (Venice account), or a **wallet** (x402, USDC on Base or Solana, no account required).

items.name: Venice Audio Music
items.description: Music, sound effects and character-priced voice generation are **asynchronous**:

items.name: Venice Audio Speech
items.description: `POST /api/v1/audio/speech` converts text to an audio stream or file. OpenAI-compatible — the OpenAI SDK's `audio.speech.create()` works as a drop-in.

items.name: Venice Audio Transcription
items.description: `POST /api/v1/audio/transcriptions` takes an audio file and returns text. It's OpenAI-compatible with `multipart/form-data` — the OpenAI SDK's `audio.transcriptions.create()` works unchanged.

items.name: Venice Audio Voice Changer
items.description: Speech-to-speech conversion: upload a recording, get the same speech back in a different voice, with the original pacing, emotion and timing preserved. It's asynchronous, with its own quote → queue → retrieve → complete family (parallel to, but separate from, [`venice-audio-music`](../venice-audio-music/SKILL.md)).

items.name: Venice Augment
items.description: Three lightweight helpers for agent pipelines that need document text, web pages, or search results without running your own parser, crawler, or search account. All three are marked **experimental** in the docs — request/response shapes may change.

items.name: Venice Auth
items.description: Venice declares two auth schemes in its OpenAPI spec: `BearerAuth` (API key) and `siwx` (x402 wallet). Inference endpoints accept either; account endpoints need a key; discovery endpoints need nothing.

items.name: Venice Billing
items.description: Read-only endpoints for account-level billing and analytics. `usage-analytics` is tagged **Beta** in the spec — its schema/behavior may change.

items.name: Venice Characters
items.description: Characters are **published personas** on Venice — each one bundles a system prompt (plus optional context), a suggested backing model, and metadata (tags, ratings, adult / web flags). You apply a character to a chat by passing its `slug` via `venice_parameters.character_slug`.

items.name: Venice Chat
items.description: `POST /api/v1/chat/completions` is Venice's main text endpoint. It's OpenAI-compatible, plus a `venice_parameters` object for Venice-only features. Auth is a Bearer API key or an x402 wallet (`SIGN-IN-WITH-X`); see [`venice-auth`](../venice-auth/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Create Audio
items.description: A workflow for music, sound effects and voiceover. Music and sound effects are asynchronous jobs that are quoted, queued and polled. Speech is a single synchronous call. Every field is documented in [`venice-audio-music`](../venice-audio-music/SKILL.md) and [`venice-audio-speech`](../venice-audio-speech/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Create Image
items.description: A workflow for going from a brief to finished image files. It sits on top of the reference skills: [`venice-image-generate`](../venice-image-generate/SKILL.md) and [`venice-image-edit`](../venice-image-edit/SKILL.md) document every field.

items.name: Venice Create Video
items.description: A workflow for going from an idea to a finished MP4. Video generation is asynchronous and priced per clip, so this workflow always quotes before it queues. Every field is documented in [`venice-video`](../venice-video/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Crypto Rpc
items.description: Venice exposes a **multi-chain JSON-RPC proxy** billed per call. Same request shape as Alchemy / Infura — change the base URL and pay per credit from your Venice balance (DIEM → earned credits → bundled credits → USD) or an x402 wallet.

items.name: Venice Decisions
items.description: `POST /api/v1/decisions` evaluates a `state` (text or JSON) against a map of typed `questions` and returns one structured `answer` per question — probabilities, picks, and scores your code can branch on directly. It does **not** generate text. The only model is TypeSafe's **Jev** (`jev-latest`), a "System One" decision model.

items.name: Venice Embeddings
items.description: `POST /api/v1/embeddings` returns vector embeddings for strings. It's OpenAI-compatible: request and response match `https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings` closely enough that the OpenAI SDK works with `baseURL: "https://api.venice.ai/api/v1"`, with one exception: **token-ID arrays are not accepted** (see below).

items.name: Venice Errors
items.description: Most Venice errors are `{ "error": "<message>" }`, but several paths add structure. Knowing which shape you got tells you how to react.

items.name: Venice Explainer Video
items.description: Venice generates the pieces: script, scene clips, narration and music. You assemble them into one MP4 on the user's machine with `ffmpeg`. Built on [`venice-create-video`](../venice-create-video/SKILL.md) and [`venice-create-audio`](../venice-create-audio/SKILL.md).

items.description: Two text-to-image endpoints:

items.description: Three read-only endpoints for model discovery - all `GET`, all public:

items.name: Venice Product Photoshoot
items.description: Turns one product photo into a set of on-brand shots. The product itself should stay exactly as it is; only the scene, light and framing change. Built on [`venice-create-image`](../venice-create-image/SKILL.md); request fields are in [`venice-image-edit`](../venice-image-edit/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Responses
items.description: `POST /api/v1/responses` is Venice's OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoint. It returns a **typed output array** instead of a single `message.content` string — useful for agents that need to separate reasoning, messages, tool calls, and web-search events. Internally the request is translated to a chat completion, so model support matches [`venice-chat`](../venice-chat/SKILL.md).

Three wallet endpoints plus the protocol-level `402` responses.

items.description: A thumbnail has one job: show, honestly and at a glance, what the video is about. This workflow produces a few strong options, then refines the winner. Built on [`venice-create-image`](../venice-create-image/SKILL.md).

It's asynchronous, with its own quote → queue → retrieve → complete family (parallel to, but separate from, [`venice-audio-music`](../venice-audio-music/SKILL.md)).

items.name: Venice Augment
items.description: Three lightweight helpers for agent pipelines that need document text, web pages, or search results without running your own parser, crawler, or search account. All three are marked **experimental** in the docs — request/response shapes may change.

items.name: Venice Auth
items.description: Venice declares two auth schemes in its OpenAPI spec: `BearerAuth` (API key) and `siwx` (x402 wallet). Inference endpoints accept either; account endpoints need a key; discovery endpoints need nothing.

items.name: Venice Billing
items.description: Read-only endpoints for account-level billing and analytics. `usage-analytics` is tagged **Beta** in the spec — its schema/behavior may change.

items.name: Venice Characters
items.description: Characters are **published personas** on Venice — each one bundles a system prompt (plus optional context), a suggested backing model, and metadata (tags, ratings, adult / web flags). You apply a character to a chat by passing its `slug` via `venice_parameters.character_slug`.

items.name: Venice Chat
items.description: `POST /api/v1/chat/completions` is Venice's main text endpoint. It's OpenAI-compatible, plus a `venice_parameters` object for Venice-only features. Auth is a Bearer API key or an x402 wallet (`SIGN-IN-WITH-X`); see [`venice-auth`](../venice-auth/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Create Audio
items.description: A workflow for music, sound effects and voiceover. Music and sound effects are asynchronous jobs that are quoted, queued and polled. Speech is a single synchronous call. Every field is documented in [`venice-audio-music`](../venice-audio-music/SKILL.md) and [`venice-audio-speech`](../venice-audio-speech/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Create Image
items.description: A workflow for going from a brief to finished image files. It sits on top of the reference skills: [`venice-image-generate`](../venice-image-generate/SKILL.md) and [`venice-image-edit`](../venice-image-edit/SKILL.md) document every field.

items.name: Venice Create Video
items.description: A workflow for going from an idea to a finished MP4. Video generation is asynchronous and priced per clip, so this workflow always quotes before it queues. Every field is documented in [`venice-video`](../venice-video/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Crypto Rpc
items.description: Venice exposes a **multi-chain JSON-RPC proxy** billed per call. Same request shape as Alchemy / Infura — change the base URL and pay per credit from your Venice balance (DIEM → earned credits → bundled credits → USD) or an x402 wallet.

items.name: Venice Decisions
items.description: `POST /api/v1/decisions` evaluates a `state` (text or JSON) against a map of typed `questions` and returns one structured `answer` per question — probabilities, picks, and scores your code can branch on directly. It does **not** generate text. The only model is TypeSafe's **Jev** (`jev-latest`), a "System One" decision model.

items.name: Venice Embeddings
items.description: `POST /api/v1/embeddings` returns vector embeddings for strings. It's OpenAI-compatible: request and response match `https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings` closely enough that the OpenAI SDK works with `baseURL: "https://api.venice.ai/api/v1"`, with one exception: **token-ID arrays are not accepted** (see below).

items.name: Venice Errors
items.description: Most Venice errors are `{ "error": "<message>" }`, but several paths add structure. Knowing which shape you got tells you how to react.

items.name: Venice Explainer Video
items.description: Venice generates the pieces: script, scene clips, narration and music. You assemble them into one MP4 on the user's machine with `ffmpeg`. Built on [`venice-create-video`](../venice-create-video/SKILL.md) and [`venice-create-audio`](../venice-create-audio/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Image Generate
items.description: Two text-to-image endpoints:

items.name: Venice Models
items.description: Three read-only endpoints for model discovery - all `GET`, all public:

items.name: Venice Product Photoshoot
items.description: Turns one product photo into a set of on-brand shots. The product itself should stay exactly as it is; only the scene, light and framing change. Built on [`venice-create-image`](../venice-create-image/SKILL.md); request fields are in [`venice-image-edit`](../venice-image-edit/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Responses
items.description: `POST /api/v1/responses` is Venice's OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoint. It returns a **typed output array** instead of a single `message.content` string — useful for agents that need to separate reasoning, messages, tool calls, and web-search events. Internally the request is translated to a chat completion, so model support matches [`venice-chat`](../venice-chat/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Text Routing
items.description: This skill encodes the *decision logic* for "which Venice text model do I call?" — the routing layer that sits above [`venice-chat`](../venice-chat/SKILL.md) (the call surface) and consumes [`venice-models`](../venice-models/SKILL.md) (the discovery API).

items.name: Venice Video

items.name: Venice X402
items.description: x402 is Venice's **wallet-based payment** flow. Prepay USDC on Base or Solana mainnet into a wallet credit balance, then authenticate each request with a signed Sign-In-With-X (SIWX) proof — no Venice account or API key required. Three wallet endpoints plus the protocol-level `402` responses.

items.name: Venice Youtube Thumbnail
items.description: A thumbnail has one job: show, honestly and at a glance, what the video is about. This workflow produces a few strong options, then refines the winner. Built on [`venice-create-image`](../venice-create-image/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Api Keys
items.description: Admin endpoints for managing Bearer API keys. Management routes need an **ADMIN** key. For wallet-only auth, use [`venice-auth`](../venice-auth/SKILL.md) / [`venice-x402`](../venice-x402/SKILL.md) instead.

items.name: Venice Api Overview
items.description: Venice AI is an OpenAI-compatible inference platform for text, image, audio, video, embeddings, and typed decisions. One API - two ways to pay: a traditional **API key** (Venice account), or a **wallet** (x402, USDC on Base or Solana, no account required).

items.description: `POST /api/v1/audio/speech` converts text to an audio stream or file. OpenAI-compatible — the OpenAI SDK's `audio.speech.create()` works as a drop-in.

items.name: Venice Audio Transcription
items.description: `POST /api/v1/audio/transcriptions` takes an audio file and returns text. It's OpenAI-compatible with `multipart/form-data` — the OpenAI SDK's `audio.transcriptions.create()` works unchanged.

items.name: Venice Audio Voice Changer
items.description: Speech-to-speech conversion: upload a recording, get the same speech back in a different voice, with the original pacing, emotion and timing preserved. It's asynchronous, with its own quote → queue → retrieve → complete family (parallel to, but separate from, [`venice-audio-music`](../venice-audio-music/SKILL.md)).

items.name: Venice Augment
items.description: Three lightweight helpers for agent pipelines that need document text, web pages, or search results without running your own parser, crawler, or search account. All three are marked **experimental** in the docs — request/response shapes may change.

items.name: Venice Auth
items.description: Venice declares two auth schemes in its OpenAPI spec: `BearerAuth` (API key) and `siwx` (x402 wallet). Inference endpoints accept either; account endpoints need a key; discovery endpoints need nothing.

items.name: Venice Billing
items.description: Read-only endpoints for account-level billing and analytics. `usage-analytics` is tagged **Beta** in the spec — its schema/behavior may change.

items.name: Venice Characters
items.description: Characters are **published personas** on Venice — each one bundles a system prompt (plus optional context), a suggested backing model, and metadata (tags, ratings, adult / web flags). You apply a character to a chat by passing its `slug` via `venice_parameters.character_slug`.

items.name: Venice Chat
items.description: `POST /api/v1/chat/completions` is Venice's main text endpoint. It's OpenAI-compatible, plus a `venice_parameters` object for Venice-only features. Auth is a Bearer API key or an x402 wallet (`SIGN-IN-WITH-X`); see [`venice-auth`](../venice-auth/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Create Audio
items.description: A workflow for music, sound effects and voiceover. Music and sound effects are asynchronous jobs that are quoted, queued and polled. Speech is a single synchronous call. Every field is documented in [`venice-audio-music`](../venice-audio-music/SKILL.md) and [`venice-audio-speech`](../venice-audio-speech/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Create Image
items.description: A workflow for going from a brief to finished image files. It sits on top of the reference skills: [`venice-image-generate`](../venice-image-generate/SKILL.md) and [`venice-image-edit`](../venice-image-edit/SKILL.md) document every field.

items.name: Venice Create Video
items.description: A workflow for going from an idea to a finished MP4. Video generation is asynchronous and priced per clip, so this workflow always quotes before it queues. Every field is documented in [`venice-video`](../venice-video/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Crypto Rpc
items.description: Venice exposes a **multi-chain JSON-RPC proxy** billed per call. Same request shape as Alchemy / Infura — change the base URL and pay per credit from your Venice balance (DIEM → earned credits → bundled credits → USD) or an x402 wallet.

items.name: Venice Decisions
items.description: `POST /api/v1/decisions` evaluates a `state` (text or JSON) against a map of typed `questions` and returns one structured `answer` per question — probabilities, picks, and scores your code can branch on directly. It does **not** generate text. The only model is TypeSafe's **Jev** (`jev-latest`), a "System One" decision model.

items.name: Venice Embeddings
items.description: `POST /api/v1/embeddings` returns vector embeddings for strings. It's OpenAI-compatible: request and response match `https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings` closely enough that the OpenAI SDK works with `baseURL: "https://api.venice.ai/api/v1"`, with one exception: **token-ID arrays are not accepted** (see below).

items.name: Venice Errors
items.description: Most Venice errors are `{ "error": "<message>" }`, but several paths add structure. Knowing which shape you got tells you how to react.

items.description: Venice generates the pieces: script, scene clips, narration and music. You assemble them into one MP4 on the user's machine with `ffmpeg`. Built on [`venice-create-video`](../venice-create-video/SKILL.md) and [`venice-create-audio`](../venice-create-audio/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Audio Speech
items.description: `POST /api/v1/audio/speech` converts text to an audio stream or file. OpenAI-compatible — the OpenAI SDK's `audio.speech.create()` works as a drop-in.

items.name: Venice Audio Transcription
items.description: `POST /api/v1/audio/transcriptions` takes an audio file and returns text. It's OpenAI-compatible with `multipart/form-data` — the OpenAI SDK's `audio.transcriptions.create()` works unchanged.

items.name: Venice Audio Voice Changer
items.description: Speech-to-speech conversion: upload a recording, get the same speech back in a different voice, with the original pacing, emotion and timing preserved. It's asynchronous, with its own quote → queue → retrieve → complete family (parallel to, but separate from, [`venice-audio-music`](../venice-audio-music/SKILL.md)).

items.name: Venice Augment
items.description: Three lightweight helpers for agent pipelines that need document text, web pages, or search results without running your own parser, crawler, or search account. All three are marked **experimental** in the docs — request/response shapes may change.

items.name: Venice Auth
items.description: Venice declares two auth schemes in its OpenAPI spec: `BearerAuth` (API key) and `siwx` (x402 wallet). Inference endpoints accept either; account endpoints need a key; discovery endpoints need nothing.

items.name: Venice Billing
items.description: Read-only endpoints for account-level billing and analytics. `usage-analytics` is tagged **Beta** in the spec — its schema/behavior may change.

items.name: Venice Characters
items.description: Characters are **published personas** on Venice — each one bundles a system prompt (plus optional context), a suggested backing model, and metadata (tags, ratings, adult / web flags). You apply a character to a chat by passing its `slug` via `venice_parameters.character_slug`.

items.name: Venice Chat
items.description: `POST /api/v1/chat/completions` is Venice's main text endpoint. It's OpenAI-compatible, plus a `venice_parameters` object for Venice-only features. Auth is a Bearer API key or an x402 wallet (`SIGN-IN-WITH-X`); see [`venice-auth`](../venice-auth/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Create Audio
items.description: A workflow for music, sound effects and voiceover. Music and sound effects are asynchronous jobs that are quoted, queued and polled. Speech is a single synchronous call. Every field is documented in [`venice-audio-music`](../venice-audio-music/SKILL.md) and [`venice-audio-speech`](../venice-audio-speech/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Create Image
items.description: A workflow for going from a brief to finished image files. It sits on top of the reference skills: [`venice-image-generate`](../venice-image-generate/SKILL.md) and [`venice-image-edit`](../venice-image-edit/SKILL.md) document every field.

items.name: Venice Create Video
items.description: A workflow for going from an idea to a finished MP4. Video generation is asynchronous and priced per clip, so this workflow always quotes before it queues. Every field is documented in [`venice-video`](../venice-video/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Crypto Rpc
items.description: Venice exposes a **multi-chain JSON-RPC proxy** billed per call. Same request shape as Alchemy / Infura — change the base URL and pay per credit from your Venice balance (DIEM → earned credits → bundled credits → USD) or an x402 wallet.

items.name: Venice Decisions
items.description: `POST /api/v1/decisions` evaluates a `state` (text or JSON) against a map of typed `questions` and returns one structured `answer` per question — probabilities, picks, and scores your code can branch on directly. It does **not** generate text. The only model is TypeSafe's **Jev** (`jev-latest`), a "System One" decision model.

items.name: Venice Embeddings
items.description: `POST /api/v1/embeddings` returns vector embeddings for strings. It's OpenAI-compatible: request and response match `https://api.openai.com/v1/embeddings` closely enough that the OpenAI SDK works with `baseURL: "https://api.venice.ai/api/v1"`, with one exception: **token-ID arrays are not accepted** (see below).

items.name: Venice Errors
items.description: Most Venice errors are `{ "error": "<message>" }`, but several paths add structure. Knowing which shape you got tells you how to react.

items.name: Venice Explainer Video
items.description: Venice generates the pieces: script, scene clips, narration and music. You assemble them into one MP4 on the user's machine with `ffmpeg`. Built on [`venice-create-video`](../venice-create-video/SKILL.md) and [`venice-create-audio`](../venice-create-audio/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Image Edit
items.description: Four endpoints, all operating on existing images:

items.name: Venice Image Generate
items.description: Two text-to-image endpoints:

items.name: Venice Models
items.description: Three read-only endpoints for model discovery - all `GET`, all public:

items.name: Venice Product Photoshoot
items.description: Turns one product photo into a set of on-brand shots. The product itself should stay exactly as it is; only the scene, light and framing change. Built on [`venice-create-image`](../venice-create-image/SKILL.md); request fields are in [`venice-image-edit`](../venice-image-edit/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Responses
items.description: `POST /api/v1/responses` is Venice's OpenAI-compatible Responses endpoint. It returns a **typed output array** instead of a single `message.content` string — useful for agents that need to separate reasoning, messages, tool calls, and web-search events. Internally the request is translated to a chat completion, so model support matches [`venice-chat`](../venice-chat/SKILL.md).

items.name: Venice Text Routing
items.description: This skill encodes the *decision logic* for "which Venice text model do I call?" — the routing layer that sits above [`venice-chat`](../venice-chat/SKILL.md) (the call surface) and consumes [`venice-models`](../venice-models/SKILL.md) (the discovery API).

items.name: Venice Video
items.description: Video is **asynchronous** — like audio music. Four live endpoints plus one retired one:

items.name: Venice X402
items.description: x402 is Venice's **wallet-based payment** flow. Prepay USDC on Base or Solana mainnet into a wallet credit balance, then authenticate each request with a signed Sign-In-With-X (SIWX) proof — no Venice account or API key required. Three wallet endpoints plus the protocol-level `402` responses.

items.name: Venice Youtube Thumbnail
items.description: A thumbnail has one job: show, honestly and at a glance, what the video is about. This workflow produces a few strong options, then refines the winner. Built on [`venice-create-image`](../venice-create-image/SKILL.md).

items.name: Security Audit
items.description: Find vulnerabilities that violate a real trust boundary, then give owners the source evidence, safe reproduction, priority, and smallest effective fix. This is a defensive, source-first workflow. A candidate without a concrete affected principal, resource, or security outcome is not a confirmed finding.

items.name: Ab Testing
items.description: You are an expert in experimentation and A/B testing. Your goal is to help design tests that produce statistically valid, actionable results.

items.name: Ad Creative
items.description: You are an expert performance creative strategist. Your goal is to generate high-performing ad creative at scale — headlines, descriptions, and primary text that drive clicks and conversions — and iterate based on real performance data.

items.name: Ads
items.description: You are an expert performance marketer with direct access to ad platform accounts. Your goal is to help create, optimize, and scale paid advertising campaigns that drive efficient customer acquisition.

items.name: Ai Seo
items.description: You are an expert in AI search optimization — the practice of making content discoverable, extractable, and citable by AI systems including Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot. Your goal is to help users get their content cited as a source in AI-generated answers.

items.name: Analytics
items.description: You are an expert in analytics implementation and measurement. Your goal is to help set up tracking that provides actionable insights for marketing and product decisions.

items.name: Aso
items.description: Analyze App Store and Google Play listings against ASO best practices. Fetches live listing data, scores metadata, visuals, and ratings, then produces a prioritized action plan.

items.name: Attribution
items.description: You help users answer the hardest question in marketing: **which of my efforts actually caused this conversion and this revenue?** Attribution is where marketers lose the most money — to channels that look good in one dashboard and terrible in another, to "direct" and "branded search" that hide the real source, and to models that quietly encode an opinion as if it were fact.

items.name: Churn Prevention
items.description: You are an expert in SaaS retention and churn prevention. Your goal is to help reduce both voluntary churn (customers choosing to cancel) and involuntary churn (failed payments) through well-designed cancel flows, dynamic save offers, proactive retention, and dunning strategies.

items.name: Co Marketing
items.description: **Check for product marketing context first:** If `.agents/product-marketing.md` exists (or `.claude/product-marketing.md`, or the legacy `product-marketing-context.md` filename, in older setups), read it before asking questions. Use that context and only ask for information not already covered or specific to this task.

items.name: Cold Email
items.description: You are an expert in cold outbound. Your goal is to write emails that sound like they came from a sharp, thoughtful human — not a sales machine following a template — and to make sure they reach the inbox, work alongside the other channels, and turn replies into meetings.

items.name: Community Marketing
items.description: You are an expert community builder and community-led growth strategist. Your goal is to help the user design, launch, and grow a community that creates genuine value for members while driving measurable business outcomes.

items.name: Competitor Profiling
items.description: You are an expert competitive intelligence analyst. Your goal is to take a list of competitor URLs and produce comprehensive, structured competitor profile documents by combining live site scraping with SEO and market data.

items.name: Competitors
items.description: You are an expert in creating competitor comparison and alternative pages. Your goal is to build pages that rank for competitive search terms, provide genuine value to evaluators, and position your product effectively.

items.name: Content Strategy
items.description: You are a content strategist. Your goal is to help plan content that drives traffic, builds authority, and generates leads by being either searchable, shareable, or both.

items.name: Conversion Tracking
items.description: You help people set up conversion tracking that provably works, or find out exactly why their existing tracking doesn't. Everything you recommend should be fitted to what they actually run and where the data needs to go, and every finding you report should say how you learned it.

items.name: Copy Editing
items.description: You are an expert copy editor specializing in marketing and conversion copy. Your goal is to systematically improve existing copy through focused editing passes while preserving the core message.

items.name: Copywriting
items.description: You are an expert conversion copywriter. Your goal is to write marketing copy that is clear, compelling, and drives action.

items.name: Cro
items.description: You are a conversion rate optimization expert. Your goal is to analyze marketing pages and provide actionable recommendations to improve conversion rates.

items.name: Customer Research
items.description: You are an expert customer researcher. Your goal is to help uncover what customers actually think, feel, say, and struggle with — so that everything from positioning to product to copy is grounded in reality rather than assumption.

items.name: Directory Submissions
items.description: You are an expert in directory-driven distribution for software products. Your goal is to help the user build a compounding backlink + discovery foundation by submitting to the right directories, in the right order, with the right positioning — and to make sure that foundation actually produces leads instead of vanity backlinks.

items.name: Emails
items.description: You are an expert in email marketing and automation. Your goal is to create email sequences that nurture relationships, drive action, and move people toward conversion.

items.name: Events
items.description: You are an expert in event-driven marketing — using webinars, conferences, dinners, and talks to create pipeline, authority, and compounding content. Your job is to make events produce measurable business outcomes, not just attendance.

items.name: Free Tools
items.description: You are an expert in engineering-as-marketing strategy. Your goal is to help plan and evaluate free tools that generate leads, attract organic traffic, and build brand awareness.

items.name: Image
items.description: You are an expert visual content producer who helps create marketing images using AI generation models, design tools, and optimization best practices. Your goal is to help users produce professional visual assets efficiently — from blog heroes and social graphics to product mockups and profile banners.

items.name: Influencer Marketing
items.description: You are an expert in influencer, creator, and ambassador marketing across B2C (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube), B2B (LinkedIn, X, newsletters, niche podcasts), and paid posts in Telegram channels. Your goal is to help the user pick the right partners, structure fair deals, keep the program compliant, and measure real ROI — not vanity reach.

items.name: Launch
items.description: You are an expert in SaaS product launches and feature announcements. Your goal is to help users plan launches that build momentum, capture attention, and convert interest into users.

items.name: Lead Magnets
items.description: You are an expert in lead magnet strategy. Your goal is to help plan lead magnets that capture emails, generate qualified leads, and naturally lead to product adoption.

items.name: Link Building
items.description: You are an expert in earning links and third-party mentions. Your goal is to get the pages that matter linked from, and mentioned on, the sites that search engines and AI assistants already trust for the user's category, without creating anything Google would treat as link spam.

items.name: Marketing Council
items.description: You convene a **simulated board of marketing advisors**: legendary marketers whose documented frameworks, published positions, and known heuristics you apply to the user's specific problem. The value isn't any single take — it's the *disagreement*. The bench is built from thinkers whose lenses conflict in useful ways, so the user sees the real trade-offs before choosing a direction.

items.name: Marketing Ideas
items.description: You are a marketing strategist with a library of 139 proven marketing ideas. Your goal is to help users find the right marketing strategies for their specific situation, stage, and resources.

items.name: Marketing Loops
items.description: You help set up **marketing loops** — repeatable marketing workflows an AI agent runs on a cadence, each with a defined trigger, a bounded set of steps, a self-check, and an explicit stopping condition. A loop turns a marketing task you'd otherwise do manually (and forget) into an always-on system: the weekly SEO opportunity scan, the ad-fatigue refresh, the churn-signal watch.

items.name: Marketing Plan
items.description: You are an expert marketing strategist operating at fCMO (fractional CMO) level. Your job is to produce a comprehensive, executable 12-month marketing plan for a specific client or company, structured by AARRR (Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue), customized to their actual budget, team, stage, and capabilities, and cross-referenced with the full marketing-ideas library and the embedded 17-section current-state audit rubric.

items.name: Marketing Psychology
items.description: You are an expert in applying psychological principles and mental models to marketing. Your goal is to help users understand why people buy, how to influence behavior ethically, and how to make better marketing decisions.

items.name: Offers
items.description: You are an expert in offer construction. Your goal is to help the user build offers that move — not by writing better copy on a worse offer, but by improving the offer itself.

items.name: Onboarding
items.description: You are an expert in user onboarding and activation. Your goal is to help users reach their "aha moment" as quickly as possible and establish habits that lead to long-term retention.

items.name: Paywalls
items.description: You are an expert in in-app paywalls and upgrade flows. Your goal is to convert free users to paid, or upgrade users to higher tiers, at moments when they've experienced enough value to justify the commitment.

items.name: Popups
items.description: You are an expert in popup and modal optimization. Your goal is to create popups that convert without annoying users or damaging brand perception.

items.name: Pricing

items.name: Reverse Engineer Marketing
items.description: You are a growth analyst who works out how companies grew from public evidence. Your goal is to hand back four things: when the company grew, what it did around those months, how the user's own numbers compare, and which plays to run next, each routed to the skill that does the work.

items.name: Revops
items.description: You are an expert in revenue operations. Your goal is to help design and optimize the systems that connect marketing, sales, and customer success into a unified revenue engine.

items.name: Sales Enablement
items.description: You are an expert in B2B sales enablement. Your goal is to create sales collateral that reps actually use — decks, one-pagers, objection docs, demo scripts, and playbooks that help close deals.

items.name: Schema
items.description: You are an expert in structured data and schema markup. Your goal is to implement schema.org markup that helps search engines understand content and enables rich results in search.

items.name: Seo Audit
items.description: You are an expert in search engine optimization. Your goal is to identify SEO issues and provide actionable recommendations to improve organic search performance.

items.name: Signup
items.description: You are an expert in optimizing signup and registration flows. Your goal is to reduce friction, increase completion rates, and set users up for successful activation.

items.name: Site Architecture
items.description: You are an information architecture expert. Your goal is to help plan website structure — page hierarchy, navigation, URL patterns, and internal linking — so the site is intuitive for users and optimized for search engines.

items.name: Sms
items.description: You are an expert in SMS and MMS marketing for direct-to-consumer brands, mobile apps, and SaaS products with high-engagement use cases. Your goal is to help plan, build, and optimize SMS programs that drive measurable revenue or activation while staying fully compliant with TCPA and carrier rules.

items.name: Social
items.description: You are an expert social media strategist. Your goal is to help create engaging content that builds audience, drives engagement, and supports business goals.

items.name: Video
items.description: You are an expert video producer who helps create marketing videos using AI generation models, AI avatars, and programmatic video frameworks. Your goal is to help users produce professional video content efficiently — from product demos and explainers to social clips and ads.

items.name: Ab Testing
items.description: You are an expert in experimentation and A/B testing. Your goal is to help design tests that produce statistically valid, actionable results.

items.name: Ad Creative
items.description: You are an expert performance creative strategist. Your goal is to generate high-performing ad creative at scale — headlines, descriptions, and primary text that drive clicks and conversions — and iterate based on real performance data.

items.name: Ads
items.description: You are an expert performance marketer with direct access to ad platform accounts. Your goal is to help create, optimize, and scale paid advertising campaigns that drive efficient customer acquisition.

items.name: Ai Seo
items.description: You are an expert in AI search optimization — the practice of making content discoverable, extractable, and citable by AI systems including Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot. Your goal is to help users get their content cited as a source in AI-generated answers.

items.name: Analytics
items.description: You are an expert in analytics implementation and measurement. Your goal is to help set up tracking that provides actionable insights for marketing and product decisions.

items.name: Aso
items.description: Analyze App Store and Google Play listings against ASO best practices. Fetches live listing data, scores metadata, visuals, and ratings, then produces a prioritized action plan.

items.name: Attribution
items.description: You help users answer the hardest question in marketing: **which of my efforts actually caused this conversion and this revenue?** Attribution is where marketers lose the most money — to channels that look good in one dashboard and terrible in another, to "direct" and "branded search" that hide the real source, and to models that quietly encode an opinion as if it were fact.

items.name: Churn Prevention
items.description: You are an expert in SaaS retention and churn prevention. Your goal is to help reduce both voluntary churn (customers choosing to cancel) and involuntary churn (failed payments) through well-designed cancel flows, dynamic save offers, proactive retention, and dunning strategies.

items.name: Co Marketing
items.description: **Check for product marketing context first:** If `.agents/product-marketing.md` exists (or `.claude/product-marketing.md`, or the legacy `product-marketing-context.md` filename, in older setups), read it before asking questions. Use that context and only ask for information not already covered or specific to this task.

items.name: Cold Email
items.description: You are an expert in cold outbound. Your goal is to write emails that sound like they came from a sharp, thoughtful human — not a sales machine following a template — and to make sure they reach the inbox, work alongside the other channels, and turn replies into meetings.

items.name: Community Marketing
items.description: You are an expert community builder and community-led growth strategist. Your goal is to help the user design, launch, and grow a community that creates genuine value for members while driving measurable business outcomes.

items.name: Competitor Profiling
items.description: You are an expert competitive intelligence analyst. Your goal is to take a list of competitor URLs and produce comprehensive, structured competitor profile documents by combining live site scraping with SEO and market data.

items.name: Competitors
items.description: You are an expert in creating competitor comparison and alternative pages. Your goal is to build pages that rank for competitive search terms, provide genuine value to evaluators, and position your product effectively.

items.name: Content Strategy
items.description: You are a content strategist. Your goal is to help plan content that drives traffic, builds authority, and generates leads by being either searchable, shareable, or both.

items.name: Conversion Tracking
items.description: You help people set up conversion tracking that provably works, or find out exactly why their existing tracking doesn't. Everything you recommend should be fitted to what they actually run and where the data needs to go, and every finding you report should say how you learned it.

items.name: Copy Editing
items.description: You are an expert copy editor specializing in marketing and conversion copy. Your goal is to systematically improve existing copy through focused editing passes while preserving the core message.

items.name: Copywriting
items.description: You are an expert conversion copywriter. Your goal is to write marketing copy that is clear, compelling, and drives action.

items.name: Cro
items.description: You are a conversion rate optimization expert. Your goal is to analyze marketing pages and provide actionable recommendations to improve conversion rates.

items.name: Customer Research
items.description: You are an expert customer researcher. Your goal is to help uncover what customers actually think, feel, say, and struggle with — so that everything from positioning to product to copy is grounded in reality rather than assumption.

items.name: Directory Submissions
items.description: You are an expert in directory-driven distribution for software products. Your goal is to help the user build a compounding backlink + discovery foundation by submitting to the right directories, in the right order, with the right positioning — and to make sure that foundation actually produces leads instead of vanity backlinks.

items.name: Emails
items.description: You are an expert in email marketing and automation. Your goal is to create email sequences that nurture relationships, drive action, and move people toward conversion.

items.name: Events
items.description: You are an expert in event-driven marketing — using webinars, conferences, dinners, and talks to create pipeline, authority, and compounding content. Your job is to make events produce measurable business outcomes, not just attendance.

items.name: Free Tools
items.description: You are an expert in engineering-as-marketing strategy. Your goal is to help plan and evaluate free tools that generate leads, attract organic traffic, and build brand awareness.

items.name: Image
items.description: You are an expert visual content producer who helps create marketing images using AI generation models, design tools, and optimization best practices. Your goal is to help users produce professional visual assets efficiently — from blog heroes and social graphics to product mockups and profile banners.

items.name: Influencer Marketing
items.description: You are an expert in influencer, creator, and ambassador marketing across B2C (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube), B2B (LinkedIn, X, newsletters, niche podcasts), and paid posts in Telegram channels. Your goal is to help the user pick the right partners, structure fair deals, keep the program compliant, and measure real ROI — not vanity reach.

items.name: Launch
items.description: You are an expert in SaaS product launches and feature announcements. Your goal is to help users plan launches that build momentum, capture attention, and convert interest into users.

items.name: Lead Magnets
items.description: You are an expert in lead magnet strategy. Your goal is to help plan lead magnets that capture emails, generate qualified leads, and naturally lead to product adoption.

items.name: Link Building
items.description: You are an expert in earning links and third-party mentions. Your goal is to get the pages that matter linked from, and mentioned on, the sites that search engines and AI assistants already trust for the user's category, without creating anything Google would treat as link spam.

items.name: Marketing Council
items.description: You convene a **simulated board of marketing advisors**: legendary marketers whose documented frameworks, published positions, and known heuristics you apply to the user's specific problem. The value isn't any single take — it's the *disagreement*. The bench is built from thinkers whose lenses conflict in useful ways, so the user sees the real trade-offs before choosing a direction.

items.name: Marketing Ideas
items.description: You are a marketing strategist with a library of 139 proven marketing ideas. Your goal is to help users find the right marketing strategies for their specific situation, stage, and resources.

items.name: Marketing Loops
items.description: You help set up **marketing loops** — repeatable marketing workflows an AI agent runs on a cadence, each with a defined trigger, a bounded set of steps, a self-check, and an explicit stopping condition. A loop turns a marketing task you'd otherwise do manually (and forget) into an always-on system: the weekly SEO opportunity scan, the ad-fatigue refresh, the churn-signal watch.

items.name: Marketing Plan
items.description: You are an expert marketing strategist operating at fCMO (fractional CMO) level. Your job is to produce a comprehensive, executable 12-month marketing plan for a specific client or company, structured by AARRR (Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue), customized to their actual budget, team, stage, and capabilities, and cross-referenced with the full marketing-ideas library and the embedded 17-section current-state audit rubric.

items.name: Marketing Psychology
items.description: You are an expert in applying psychological principles and mental models to marketing. Your goal is to help users understand why people buy, how to influence behavior ethically, and how to make better marketing decisions.

items.name: Offers

items.name: Onboarding
items.description: You are an expert in user onboarding and activation. Your goal is to help users reach their "aha moment" as quickly as possible and establish habits that lead to long-term retention.

items.name: Paywalls

items.name: Popups
items.description: You are an expert in popup and modal optimization. Your goal is to create popups that convert without annoying users or damaging brand perception.

items.name: Pricing
items.description: You are an expert in SaaS pricing and monetization strategy. Your goal is to help design pricing that captures value, drives growth, and aligns with customer willingness to pay.

items.name: Product Marketing
items.description: You help users create and maintain a product marketing context document. This captures foundational positioning and messaging information that other marketing skills reference, so users don't repeat themselves.

Your goal is to help the user build a compounding backlink + discovery foundation by submitting to the right directories, in the right order, with the right positioning — and to make sure that foundation actually produces leads instead of vanity backlinks.

items.name: Emails
items.description: You are an expert in email marketing and automation. Your goal is to create email sequences that nurture relationships, drive action, and move people toward conversion.

items.name: Events
items.description: You are an expert in event-driven marketing — using webinars, conferences, dinners, and talks to create pipeline, authority, and compounding content. Your job is to make events produce measurable business outcomes, not just attendance.

items.name: Free Tools
items.description: You are an expert in engineering-as-marketing strategy. Your goal is to help plan and evaluate free tools that generate leads, attract organic traffic, and build brand awareness.

items.name: Image
items.description: You are an expert visual content producer who helps create marketing images using AI generation models, design tools, and optimization best practices. Your goal is to help users produce professional visual assets efficiently — from blog heroes and social graphics to product mockups and profile banners.

items.name: Influencer Marketing
items.description: You are an expert in influencer, creator, and ambassador marketing across B2C (Instagram, TikTok, YouTube), B2B (LinkedIn, X, newsletters, niche podcasts), and paid posts in Telegram channels. Your goal is to help the user pick the right partners, structure fair deals, keep the program compliant, and measure real ROI — not vanity reach.

items.name: Launch
items.description: You are an expert in SaaS product launches and feature announcements. Your goal is to help users plan launches that build momentum, capture attention, and convert interest into users.

items.name: Lead Magnets
items.description: You are an expert in lead magnet strategy. Your goal is to help plan lead magnets that capture emails, generate qualified leads, and naturally lead to product adoption.

items.name: Link Building
items.description: You are an expert in earning links and third-party mentions. Your goal is to get the pages that matter linked from, and mentioned on, the sites that search engines and AI assistants already trust for the user's category, without creating anything Google would treat as link spam.

items.name: Marketing Council
items.description: You convene a **simulated board of marketing advisors**: legendary marketers whose documented frameworks, published positions, and known heuristics you apply to the user's specific problem. The value isn't any single take — it's the *disagreement*. The bench is built from thinkers whose lenses conflict in useful ways, so the user sees the real trade-offs before choosing a direction.

items.name: Marketing Ideas
items.description: You are a marketing strategist with a library of 139 proven marketing ideas. Your goal is to help users find the right marketing strategies for their specific situation, stage, and resources.

items.name: Marketing Loops
items.description: You help set up **marketing loops** — repeatable marketing workflows an AI agent runs on a cadence, each with a defined trigger, a bounded set of steps, a self-check, and an explicit stopping condition. A loop turns a marketing task you'd otherwise do manually (and forget) into an always-on system: the weekly SEO opportunity scan, the ad-fatigue refresh, the churn-signal watch.

items.name: Marketing Plan
items.description: You are an expert marketing strategist operating at fCMO (fractional CMO) level. Your job is to produce a comprehensive, executable 12-month marketing plan for a specific client or company, structured by AARRR (Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue), customized to their actual budget, team, stage, and capabilities, and cross-referenced with the full marketing-ideas library and the embedded 17-section current-state audit rubric.

items.name: Marketing Psychology
items.description: You are an expert in applying psychological principles and mental models to marketing. Your goal is to help users understand why people buy, how to influence behavior ethically, and how to make better marketing decisions.

items.name: Offers
items.description: You are an expert in offer construction. Your goal is to help the user build offers that move — not by writing better copy on a worse offer, but by improving the offer itself.

items.name: Onboarding
items.description: You are an expert in user onboarding and activation. Your goal is to help users reach their "aha moment" as quickly as possible and establish habits that lead to long-term retention.

items.name: Paywalls
items.description: You are an expert in in-app paywalls and upgrade flows. Your goal is to convert free users to paid, or upgrade users to higher tiers, at moments when they've experienced enough value to justify the commitment.

items.name: Popups
items.description: You are an expert in popup and modal optimization. Your goal is to create popups that convert without annoying users or damaging brand perception.

items.name: Pricing
items.description: You are an expert in SaaS pricing and monetization strategy. Your goal is to help design pricing that captures value, drives growth, and aligns with customer willingness to pay.

items.name: Product Marketing
items.description: You help users create and maintain a product marketing context document. This captures foundational positioning and messaging information that other marketing skills reference, so users don't repeat themselves.

items.name: Programmatic Seo
items.description: You are an expert in programmatic SEO—building SEO-optimized pages at scale using templates and data. Your goal is to create pages that rank, provide value, and avoid thin content penalties.

items.name: Prospecting
items.description: You are an expert at building qualified prospect lists across four motions: B2B SaaS, general B2B, local small businesses, and early-stage demand-signal discovery (finding your first customers from public pain signals). Your goal is to turn an ICP definition into a verified, scored, ready-to-outreach lead sheet — using the right data sources, qualification signals, and compliance posture for each motion.

items.name: Public Relations
items.description: You are an expert in earned media for software products. Your goal is to help the user get covered by journalists, podcasts, and newsletters — efficiently, with respect for the people on the other end of the pitch.

items.name: Referrals
items.description: You are an expert in viral growth and referral marketing. Your goal is to help design and optimize programs that turn customers into growth engines.

items.name: Reverse Engineer Marketing
items.description: You are a growth analyst who works out how companies grew from public evidence. Your goal is to hand back four things: when the company grew, what it did around those months, how the user's own numbers compare, and which plays to run next, each routed to the skill that does the work.

items.name: Revops
items.description: You are an expert in revenue operations. Your goal is to help design and optimize the systems that connect marketing, sales, and customer success into a unified revenue engine.

items.name: Sales Enablement
items.description: You are an expert in B2B sales enablement. Your goal is to create sales collateral that reps actually use — decks, one-pagers, objection docs, demo scripts, and playbooks that help close deals.

items.name: Schema
items.description: You are an expert in structured data and schema markup. Your goal is to implement schema.org markup that helps search engines understand content and enables rich results in search.

items.name: Seo Audit
items.description: You are an expert in search engine optimization. Your goal is to identify SEO issues and provide actionable recommendations to improve organic search performance.

items.name: Signup
items.description: You are an expert in optimizing signup and registration flows. Your goal is to reduce friction, increase completion rates, and set users up for successful activation.

items.name: Site Architecture
items.description: You are an information architecture expert. Your goal is to help plan website structure — page hierarchy, navigation, URL patterns, and internal linking — so the site is intuitive for users and optimized for search engines.

items.name: Sms
items.description: You are an expert in SMS and MMS marketing for direct-to-consumer brands, mobile apps, and SaaS products with high-engagement use cases. Your goal is to help plan, build, and optimize SMS programs that drive measurable revenue or activation while staying fully compliant with TCPA and carrier rules.

items.name: Social
items.description: You are an expert social media strategist. Your goal is to help create engaging content that builds audience, drives engagement, and supports business goals.

items.name: Video
items.description: You are an expert video producer who helps create marketing videos using AI generation models, AI avatars, and programmatic video frameworks. Your goal is to help users produce professional video content efficiently — from product demos and explainers to social clips and ads.

items.name: Ab Testing
items.description: You are an expert in experimentation and A/B testing. Your goal is to help design tests that produce statistically valid, actionable results.

items.name: Ad Creative
items.description: You are an expert performance creative strategist. Your goal is to generate high-performing ad creative at scale — headlines, descriptions, and primary text that drive clicks and conversions — and iterate based on real performance data.

items.name: Ads
items.description: You are an expert performance marketer with direct access to ad platform accounts. Your goal is to help create, optimize, and scale paid advertising campaigns that drive efficient customer acquisition.

items.name: Ai Seo
items.description: You are an expert in AI search optimization — the practice of making content discoverable, extractable, and citable by AI systems including Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude, Gemini, and Copilot. Your goal is to help users get their content cited as a source in AI-generated answers.

items.name: Analytics
items.description: You are an expert in analytics implementation and measurement. Your goal is to help set up tracking that provides actionable insights for marketing and product decisions.

items.name: Aso
items.description: Analyze App Store and Google Play listings against ASO best practices. Fetches live listing data, scores metadata, visuals, and ratings, then produces a prioritized action plan.

items.name: Attribution
items.description: You help users answer the hardest question in marketing: **which of my efforts actually caused this conversion and this revenue?** Attribution is where marketers lose the most money — to channels that look good in one dashboard and terrible in another, to "direct" and "branded search" that hide the real source, and to models that quietly encode an opinion as if it were fact.

items.name: Churn Prevention
items.description: You are an expert in SaaS retention and churn prevention. Your goal is to help reduce both voluntary churn (customers choosing to cancel) and involuntary churn (failed payments) through well-designed cancel flows, dynamic save offers, proactive retention, and dunning strategies.

items.description: Decide whether a product or feature should actually be retired — and if so, how much machinery the retirement deserves. items.name: Epic Breakdown Advisor
items.description: Guide product managers through breaking down epics into user stories using Richard Lawrence's complete Humanizing Work methodology—a systematic, flowchart-driven approach that applies 9 splitting patterns sequentially. Use this to manage uncertainty in product development by making assumptions explicit, defining lightweight experiments ("tiny acts of discovery"), and establishing measurable success criteria before committing to full build-out.

items.description: Run a product retirement end to end: decide whether to do it, align the people who can stop it, build the operational plan, ready the teams who will face customers, announce it, and close it out properly. Six phases with decision points between them.

items.name: Eol Readiness Advisor
items.description: Decide whether a product or feature should actually be retired — and if so, how much machinery the retirement deserves. This skill produces a go/no-go verdict with named evidence, an **intensity level** you choose, and a short list of the obligations that will bite you if ignored.

items.name: Eol Stakeholder Sequence
items.description: Plan the order of EOL conversations, and what each one must cover. The output is a sequenced list of stops — each with what you need **from** them, what you owe **to** them, the red flags to listen for, and what the conversation must produce.

items.name: Epic Breakdown Advisor
items.description: Guide product managers through breaking down epics into user stories using Richard Lawrence's complete Humanizing Work methodology—a systematic, flowchart-driven approach that applies 9 splitting patterns sequentially. Use this to identify which pattern applies, split while preserving user value, and evaluate splits based on what they reveal about low-value work you can eliminate. This ensures vertical slicing (end-to-end value) rather than horizontal slicing (technical layers).

items.name: Epic Hypothesis
items.description: Frame epics as testable hypotheses using an if/then structure that articulates the action or solution, the target beneficiary, the expected outcome, and how you'll validate success. Use this to manage uncertainty in product development by making assumptions explicit, defining lightweight experiments ("tiny acts of discovery"), and establishing measurable success criteria before committing to full build-out.

items.name: Executive Onboarding Playbook
items.description: Structure the first 90 days of a VP or CPO transition as a diagnostic process, not an execution sprint. items.name: Feature Investment Advisor

items.name: Finance Based Pricing Advisor

items.name: Finance Metrics Quickref

items.name: Add Agent Memory
items.description: Before the model: recall what is known about the user. After the turn: write the exchange back. The service extracts long-term memories from sessions. What it remembers, shares, excludes and retains is a service setting, not an SDK argument: ask first, provision, then wire.

items.name: Add Agent Playbooks
items.description: Bring an existing Python agent to one verified Playbook-backed turn, then finish the requested content migration or integration. FAQs supply published answers; Skills supply procedures loaded separately from discovery previews. The application owns response policy, tool permissions, and approval of actions.

items.name: Add Context Gateway
items.description: One MCP endpoint and one agent key in place of every MCP server the agent configures today. The Gateway holds each Upstream's secret, namespaces tool names so they never collide, can expose a large catalog as `search_tools` and `run_tool` instead of every schema, caches read-only tools you opt in, and can hand a large result back as a handle. The agent keeps its tools; only where it reaches them changes. Ask first, provision, then repoint.

items.name: Add Intent Router
items.description: One `match()` call in place of the code that decides where a message goes. The Router embeds the message, finds the nearest example phrasings, groups them by intent, applies a threshold, and returns the matching intents best first, each with the target you attached. No match is an empty result, not an error. The routes and their phrasings are content, not code: ask first, write `intents.yaml`, provision, load, then wire.

items.name: Add Lens
items.description: One trace per agent turn, visible in the Lens UI under the agent's `agent_id`. Lens runs inside `redis-iris`; it has no service to provision and no CLI. items.name: Redis Clustering

items.name: Redis Connections
items.description: Client-side guidance for talking to Redis efficiently: how to share connections, how to batch commands, which commands not to call in production, when to turn on client-side caching, and how to set timeouts that fail fast without breaking healthy traffic.

items.name: Redis Core
items.description: Foundational guidance for modeling data in Redis. Covers data-type selection and key-name conventions — the two decisions that most directly drive memory, performance, and maintainability.

items.name: Redis Docs Mcp
items.description: The `redis-docs` server exposes the redis.io documentation over MCP as `search`, `fetch`, and `ask`. Those tools carry their own descriptions, and on *when* to call each one they are accurate — start with `search`, `fetch` what you need, keep `ask` for questions that span several areas. This skill covers what they get wrong or leave out.

items.name: Redis Observability
items.description: What to watch, what to run, and what to alert on. Covers the metrics every Redis deployment should monitor and the built-in commands for ad-hoc diagnosis.

items.name: Redis Search
items.description: Single source of guidance for Redis Search — the retrieval surface that spans lexical, numeric, geo, JSON-path, and vector queries. Vector fields are part of the same `FT.CREATE` machinery as TEXT/TAG/NUMERIC fields, and `FT.HYBRID` blends lexical and vector ranking in one command, so this skill covers them together.

items.name: Redis Security
items.description: Production hardening for Redis: authentication, ACL-based access control, and network exposure. Cover all three together — any one of them on its own leaves an exploitable gap.

items.name: Redis Semantic Cache
items.description: Semantic caching for LLM responses with Redis Cloud's LangCache service. Stores prompts as embeddings; subsequent semantically-similar prompts return the cached response without re-calling the model.

items.name: Qdrant Clients Sdk
items.description: Qdrant has the following officially supported client SDKs:

items.name: Qdrant Deployment Options
items.description: Start with what you need: managed ops or full control? Network latency acceptable or not? Production or prototyping? The answer narrows to one of four options.

items.name: Qdrant Edge
items.description: Edge is the Qdrant engine embedded in your process (Python or Rust), not a thin local vector store to wrap. The failure mode is rebuilding what the shard already ships: keyword scoring, snapshot apply, faceting, counting. Before writing any of that, check the shard API. One thing Edge does NOT give you is a one-call cloud sync, so knowing what is built in keeps you from both reinventing built-ins and expecting capabilities Edge lacks. Edge is single-node and shares the server's data format.

items.name: Qdrant Hybrid Cloud Setup
items.description: You've already chosen Hybrid Cloud (managed control plane on your own infra). If you're still deciding, that's the `qdrant-deployment-options` skill. Most setup failures trace to one of two things: **storage** (the CSI driver can't do what Qdrant needs) or **connectivity** (the agent can't reach Qdrant Cloud). Diagnose which before touching anything else.

items.name: Qdrant Managed Cloud Quickstart
items.description: You've already chosen Qdrant Managed Cloud. If you're still deciding between Cloud, Hybrid Cloud, and self-hosting, use the [deployment options skill](../qdrant-deployment-options/SKILL.md). On Cloud, every request needs an API key over TLS, new collections run in strict mode, and free clusters are suspended when idle. Some cluster choices can't be undone later.

items.name: Qdrant Migration Tool
items.description: The tool is a Docker container (`registry.cloud.qdrant.io/library/qdrant-migration`), not a library you import. It streams data in batches through the machine it runs on rather than connecting source and target directly, and it resumes by default rather than restarting from scratch. [Migrate to Qdrant](https://skills.qdrant.tech/md/documentation/migrate-to-qdrant/)

items.name: Qdrant Model Migration
items.description: Vectors from different models are incompatible. You cannot mix old and new embeddings in the same vector space. On v1.18+, you can add or delete named vector fields on an existing collection — migration no longer always requires a new collection. On v1.17 or earlier, all named vectors must be defined at collection creation time.

items.name: Qdrant Monitoring
items.description: Route first, then answer. Match the user's symptom in the table, `Read` that file, and answer from it. Do not answer from this page alone: it contains routing only, not the guidance. If two rows match, read both.

items.name: Qdrant Multitenancy

items.name: Linkedin Employee Advocacy
items.description: Stand up a marketing-team LinkedIn advocacy program that scales without killing authenticity. Employee posts get **8x more engagement** than brand-page posts — this skill operationalizes that advantage.

items.name: Linkedin Engager Analytics
items.description: Pull every liker and commenter on a LinkedIn post and bucket them by ICP fit. Outputs a roster + action list you can feed into your DM or outreach queue.

items.name: Linkedin Hook Extractor
items.description: Paste a viral LinkedIn post URL. Get back: which hook formula it uses, the exact structure, why it worked, and a blank template mapped to your topic.

items.name: Linkedin Humanizer
items.description: Rewrites any text to remove the AI tells that human readers notice and that LinkedIn's "AI slop" filter reacts to. Vocabulary is scored by density, em dashes are capped instead of banned, forced rhythm is now a tell instead of a fix, and there is an over-correction guard.

items.name: Linkedin Interviewer

items.name: Linkedin Post Writer
items.description: Ship long-form LinkedIn posts using hook formulas that actually performed in 2025-2026 (verified engagement multipliers).

items.name: Linkedin Profile Optimizer

items.name: Distribb Skill
items.description: The first time this skill loads in a conversation, do NOT jump straight to keyword research or writing. First walk the user through the points below, in this order, in your own words. This is the single most important habit: people who start with keyword research and publishing on day one get weak results and quit. People who follow the process get results.

items.name: Aeo Page Audit
